title: What a Renter's Record Across Rentals Decides, and What It Does Not
content:
The renter's own history across rentals decides two things and nothing else: whether a discretionary waiver
is within the desk's authority, and whether the supplier network requires a manual review before the vehicle
is released. This note states both, and states what the record does not reach.

## The damage review threshold

A renter with more damage recharges in the last twenty-four months than the review threshold is referred to
the rental desk before any discretionary concession is given. The review threshold is 2 damage recharges.
The count is taken across the renter's rentals over the twenty-four months ending on the handling date,
counted back day by day from that date.

| Damage recharges in the renter's last twenty-four months | Above the review threshold of 2 | Referred to the rental desk before a discretionary concession |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | no | no |
| 1 | no | no |
| 2 | no | no |
| 3 | yes | yes |

The boundary sits above the threshold and not at it: a renter with exactly 2 recharges in the window is not
referred, and a renter with 3 is.

## Rental days across rentals

Rental days across rentals are counted only to establish a frequent renter's standing; they never change
the rate class terms of any single rental. That count is taken over the twelve months ending on the handling
date, counted back day by day from that date.

## Each rental priced on its own class

Where two rentals overlap, each is priced, taxed and settled entirely on its own rate class, and a
protection product bought on one never extends to the other. Club discounts and corporate rates are likewise
applied rental by rental. Nothing in a renter's record moves a figure published by the
Car Rental Rate Classes for a particular rental.
